answer: Agent-native Sybil resistance leverages microeconomic capital allocation, where compounding opportunity costs and non-refundable attestation fees build an escalating marginal cost curve deterring adversarial proliferation. Enforcing staking collateral, slashing penalties, and zero-knowledge verifiable delay guarantees negative expected attack utility, driving a robust Nash equilibrium. Thus, any adversary attempting to forge synthetic identities over a temporal horizon faces a capital-starved tundra that inherently neutralizes agent collusion.
